propositions.statement: n=λ+1>0 and e=(e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V with card(I)=n. For every integer i≥0, h y^iv=(λ−2i)y^iv, and for i≥1, x y^iv=i(λ−i+1)y^{i−1}v. Also y^{λ+1}v=0 and all higher powers vanish. On the basis e, xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_{i−1} for 1≤i≤λ, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. For all r∈ℕ and i∈I, X_re_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_{i−r} when r≤i and is zero otherwise; Y_re_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} when i+r≤λ and is zero otherwise. These binomial coefficients are integers.

Every X_r,Y_r preserves M and M_R, and x,y,h preserve M and M_R. The multiplication map R⊗_ℤ M→M_R, r⊗m↦rm, is an isomorphism. M_R is free of rank n over R and spans V over ℂ. For i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit of R and, as endomorphisms of V, Y_λX_λ=E_λλ, X_{λ−i}E_λλ=E_iλ, E_λλY_{λ−j}=binom(λ,j)E_λj and E_ij=binom(λ,j)⁻¹ X_{λ−i}Y_λX_λY_{λ−j}. Every E_ij preserves M_R.

propositions.statement: There is a ring map ρ:R→K, ρ(a/d)=(a in K)(d in K)⁻¹, and natural isomorphisms V(K)≅M_R⊗_R K≅(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{𝔽_p}K. For some nonzero b∈J with J=Rb, the images b_i of b e_i form a K-basis (b_i)_{i∈I} of V(K). Its x_K,y_K,h_K matrices are x_K b_0=0, x_K b_i=(λ−i+1)b_{i−1} for 1≤i≤λ, y_K b_i=(i+1)b_{i+1} for i<λ, y_K b_λ=0 and h_K b_i=(λ−2i)b_i, with integer coefficients mapped to K. The reductions X_{r,K},Y_{r,K} of X_r,Y_r are defined for all r≥0. For 0≤r≤λ, r! is nonzero in K and X_{r,K}=(r!)⁻¹x_K^r, Y_{r,K}=(r!)⁻¹y_K^r. For all i,j∈I, the scalar binom(λ,j) has nonzero image in K, and F_ij=ρ(binom(λ,j)⁻¹)X_{λ−i,K}Y_{λ,K}X_{λ,K}Y_{λ−j,K} sends b_j to b_i and every other b_k to zero.

propositions.statement: V(K) is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V(K), if x_K(W)⊆W, y_K(W)⊆W and h_K(W)⊆W, then W={0} or W=V(K). Thus V(K) is irreducible for the induced L(K)-action, with no exception for λ=0 or p=2 and no algebraic-closure assumption on K.

argument.text: H001 gives λ≥0, hence n=λ+1>0 and card(I)=n. We prove the two asserted commutator formulas for all nonnegative integer i by induction. At i=0 the h formula and xv=0 are H003. If the formulas hold at i, H002 gives h y^{i+1}v=(yh−2y)y^iv=(λ−2i−2)y^{i+1}v, and x y^{i+1}v=(yx+h)y^iv=[i(λ−i+1)+(λ−2i)]y^iv=(i+1)(λ−i)y^iv. This proves both inductions (the i=0 x term is zero). For 0≤i≤λ, iterating the x formula gives x^i y^iv=i! λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v, nonzero over ℂ by H003 and the positive integer factors, with empty product one at i=0. Thus e_i≠0 for each i∈I.

produces.statement: n>0, card(I)=n; for all i≥0, h y^iv=(λ−2i)y^iv, and for i≥1, x y^iv=i(λ−i+1)y^{i−1}v. Each e_i for i∈I is nonzero.

argument.text: The eigenvalues λ−2i of e_i for i∈I are distinct in ℂ by F001. For an arbitrary complex linear relation ∑_{i∈I} c_i e_i=0, apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h−(λ−2k)Id_V), for any j∈I. It kills every term but the j-th, giving c_j∏_{k≠j}2(k−j)e_j=0; the multiplier and e_j are nonzero, so c_j=0. Thus e is linearly independent. Apply M002 with A=ℂ, Z=V, T=I, d=e: I is finite nonempty by F001; independence was just proved and card(I)=n=dim_ℂ V by H002. Its span is V, so e is a basis. F001 at i=λ+1 shows that y^{λ+1}v has h-eigenvalue −λ−2 if nonzero. Expansion in this basis and comparison of coefficients in the h-eigenvector equation forces each coefficient to be zero, since −λ−2 differs from every λ−2i, i∈I. Hence y^{λ+1}v=0; further y powers are zero.

produces.statement: e is a complex basis of V. y^{λ+1}v=0 and y^tv=0 for every integer t≥λ+1.

argument.text: Dividing F001 by i! and using F002 gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_{i−1} for i≥1 in I, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. Iterating these formulas r times and dividing by r! gives X_re_i=((λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r!)e_{i−r}=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_{i−r} for r≤i, and Y_re_i=((i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!)e_{i+r}=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} for i+r≤λ. The terminating strings give zero in the other cases, including all powers beyond their endpoints. Products are empty at r=0. These coefficients are integers: binom(a,r) for natural a≥r counts r-element subsets of an a-element set (or follows from Pascal's recurrence with initial values one); this applies to both displayed upper indices. Together with F001 and F002 these prove the complete asserted output.

hypothesis_checks: ℂ is a division ring and V is its given vector space.
F001 gives card(I)=n>0, so I is finite nonempty.
S002 proves independence by applying the displayed isolating polynomial to an arbitrary relation.
F001 and H002 give card(I)=n=finrank_ℂ V.

locals.declaration: Choose the integer basis m=(m_t)_{t∈I} of M, also a complex basis of V, whose existence is F001.

argument.text: By H004 an integer basis of M is a complex basis of V. Apply M006 to that complex basis and the complex basis e of N001. Since ℂ is a field it has invariant basis number, so their index sets have equal cardinality. The latter set is the finite set I; hence the former basis may be indexed by I. Thus there exists an integer basis (m_t)_{t∈I} of M that is also a complex basis of V. This is F001.

produces.statement: There exists an integer basis m:I→M of M whose images are a complex basis of V.

argument.text: Choose such m by F001. Apply M001 with A=ℤ, Z=M, B=R and basis m. It gives the R-basis (1⊗m_t) of R⊗_ℤ M. The multiplication map sends it to (m_t) in V. These images are complex-linearly independent, hence R-linearly independent, and span M_R by definition. The map is therefore injective and has image exactly M_R, and these images give an R-basis of M_R of cardinality card(I)=n. They also show that M_R spans V over ℂ. This proves the localization identification without an implicit faithfulness assumption.

produces.statement: The multiplication map R⊗_ℤ M→M_R is an isomorphism; m is an R-basis of M_R of length n and M_R spans V over ℂ.

argument.text: H004 and the generating definition of U_ℤ show that X_r,Y_r preserve M for every r≥0. Complex linearity then shows preservation of its R-span M_R. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve both modules; h=xy−yx by H002 preserves them as well. For arbitrary i,j∈I, evaluate on each e_k using N001. X_λ is zero except on e_λ, where it gives e_0, and Y_λ e_0=e_λ. Thus Y_λX_λ=E_λλ. Next X_{λ−i}e_λ=e_i, so X_{λ−i}E_λλ=E_iλ. Finally E_λλY_{λ−j} is zero on e_k if k<j, since its image before projection is below e_λ, and if k>j, since the lowering string has terminated. On e_j its coefficient is binom(λ,j), so E_λλY_{λ−j}=binom(λ,j)E_λj.

produces.statement: All X_r,Y_r and x,y,h preserve M and M_R. For all i,j∈I, Y_λX_λ=E_λλ, X_{λ−i}E_λλ=E_iλ, and E_λλY_{λ−j}=binom(λ,j)E_λj.

argument.text: For every j∈I, H001 gives 0≤j≤λ<p. Apply M005 with prime q=p and a=λ,j,λ−j: none of λ!, j!, (λ−j)! is divisible by p. The integer identity binom(λ,j) j!(λ−j)!=λ! then implies that p cannot divide binom(λ,j). Its inverse 1/binom(λ,j) belongs to R by D007; thus the binomial coefficient is a unit of R. F003 now yields E_ij=binom(λ,j)⁻¹X_{λ−i}E_λλY_{λ−j}=binom(λ,j)⁻¹X_{λ−i}Y_λX_λY_{λ−j}. Each factor preserves M_R, and the inverse coefficient is in R, so every E_ij preserves M_R. Combine with F002 and F003 to obtain the full asserted output. No reduced weights were compared.

V is a complex vector space.
H004 supplies the first complex basis; N001 supplies e. Universe lifting does not alter the index sets or their cardinalities.

applications.bindings: A=ℤ, Z=M, B=R, T=I, d=m; the formula is applied for each t∈I.

The chosen m is an integer basis by F001, and t ranges over I.

hypothesis_checks: p is prime by H001. Each factorial argument is a natural number by H001 and j∈I.

locals.declaration: Let U be the rational span of J in ℂ.
Let T be the rational span of M_R in V.
Put r=dim_ℚ U, a finite natural number by the finite spanning set established in S002.

argument.text: N002 says every E_ij preserves M_R, and N001 supplies the basis e. The projection E_ii maps M_R onto J_i e_i. If c∈J_j, applying E_ij to c e_j gives c e_i∈M_R, so J_j⊆J_i; reversing the indices proves equality. Since 0∈I and e_0=v, their common value is J. Projecting a finite R-basis of M_R (N002) shows J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: otherwise all projections of M_R vanish, so M_R=0, contrary to its complex span V and the positive size of the basis in N001. Projection onto coordinates shows M_R=∑_{i∈I}J e_i, and complex independence of e makes the sum direct.

produces.statement: All J_i equal J. J is a nonzero finitely generated R-submodule of ℂ, and M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i.

argument.text: Let U=span_ℚ J and T=span_ℚ M_R. The multiplication map ℚ⊗_R J→U is an isomorphism, as follows directly by clearing denominators. Every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors q⊗c; a common positive integer denominator d for its rational coefficients rewrites it as (1/d)⊗c' with c'∈J. If it maps to zero in ℂ, then c'/d=0, so c'=0 and the tensor is zero. Its image is exactly U. The same argument for M_R⊆V identifies ℚ⊗_R M_R with T. A finite generating set of J spans U over ℚ; hence U has a finite basis: successively discard from that finite list every vector lying in the span of preceding retained ones, leaving an independent spanning list. The same finite selection argument applies to any finite spanning list used below. The R-basis of M_R from N002 is a ℚ-basis of T: it spans T, and any rational relation can be multiplied by a common nonzero integer denominator to give an R-relation, which is zero only with every coefficient zero. Thus T has a ℚ-basis of n elements.

produces.statement: Multiplication identifies ℚ⊗_R J injectively with U=span_ℚ J⊆ℂ, and ℚ⊗_R M_R with T=span_ℚ M_R⊆V. U has a finite ℚ-basis and T has a ℚ-basis of n elements.

argument.text: Put r=dim_ℚ U. Tensoring the coordinate decomposition in F001, or equivalently taking rational spans in V, gives T=⊕_{i∈I}U e_i: a rational combination in M_R has coordinates in U; conversely each finite combination of U-coordinates is a rational combination of the J-coordinate vectors. Independence follows from the complex independence of e in N001. For a ℚ-basis (u_s) of U and each i∈I, the vectors u_s e_i are therefore a ℚ-basis of T: expand each coordinate in u_s for spanning and compare first the e_i and then the u_s coefficients for independence. Apply M003 over ℚ to the basis of U and the two bases of T just displayed and supplied by F002. This gives dim_ℚ T=n and also dim_ℚ T=card(I)·r=nr. Since n>0 by N001, n=nr implies r=1. Thus the injective tensor map in F002 has one-dimensional image. This is the rank-one argument; containment of J in ℂ alone was not used to infer its rank.

produces.statement: dim_ℚ U=1, and the map ℚ⊗_R J→ℂ is injective with image U of dimension one.

argument.text: By F001 choose any nonzero a∈J and a finite list of nonzero R-generators of J, deleting zero generators. By F003 each generator has a unique form q_t a with q_t∈ℚ×. Write each q_t=A_t/B_t with A_t a nonzero integer and B_t a positive integer. Apply M004 to |A_t| and B_t with q=p. Its hypotheses hold because these natural numbers are nonzero and H001 gives p≥2. Thus |A_t|=p^{s_t}A'_t and B_t=p^{t_t}B'_t with p not dividing A'_t or B'_t. Consequently q_t=p^{ν_t}u_t where ν_t=s_t−t_t∈ℤ and u_t=sign(A_t)A'_t/B'_t is a unit of R, its inverse also having denominator prime to p. Let ν be the minimum of the finitely many ν_t (the list is nonempty since J≠0). Every generator lies in p^ν R a, since ν_t−ν≥0. A generator of minimum exponent is p^νu_t a and generates exactly p^ν R a because u_t is a unit. Therefore J=p^ν R a. In particular there exists nonzero b∈J with J=Rb (take that minimal generator, or p^νa). F001 now gives M_R=⊕_{i∈I}R b e_i. Its summands have independent generators because b≠0 and e is complex-linearly independent. Hence (b e_i) is an R-basis. This proves the asserted output including the tensor injection and dimension claim from F003.

applications.bindings: A=ℚ. First Z=U and d a finite basis selected from the spanning list in S002; then Z=T and d respectively the n-element basis in F002 and the product family u_s e_i indexed by I times the basis index set of U.
hypothesis_checks: ℚ is a field, hence satisfies strong rank condition: finite Gaussian elimination bounds the number of independent column vectors by the number of rows.
U and T are rational subspaces, so are additive commutative groups with ℚ-module structures.
F002 supplies finite bases; S003 proves directly that the product family is a finite basis.

applications.bindings: For each nonzero generator q_t a of J and rational presentation q_t=A_t/B_t with B_t>0, set q=p and set a=|A_t| and then a=B_t.
hypothesis_checks: A_t≠0 and B_t>0 by the chosen presentation of a nonzero rational, hence the two natural numbers are nonzero.
p≥2 by H001, in particular p≠1.

locals.declaration: Define ρ(a/d)=(a in K)(d in K)⁻¹ for a,d∈ℤ and p∤d; well-definedness is proved in S001.
Choose b≠0 in J with J=Rb and (b e_i) an R-basis of M_R using N003.
For i∈I let b_i be the image of (b e_i)⊗1 under the isomorphism M_R⊗_R K→V(K) proved in F002.

argument.text: By H001 an integer d not divisible by p has nonzero image in K: division with remainder by the characteristic p shows an integer has zero image exactly when divisible by p. Thus its image is invertible. Define ρ(a/d)=(a in K)(d in K)⁻¹ on R. Equality a/d=a'/d' is ad'=a'd, which remains true after mapping integers to K, so this definition is well-defined and preserves sums, products and one by the fraction formulas. In particular all R-denominators act invertibly. The same formula into 𝔽_p identifies R/pR with 𝔽_p: it is onto because integers map onto 𝔽_p, and its kernel consists of fractions with numerator divisible by p, exactly pR. The induced map 𝔽_p→K is injective because it is unital between fields. These maps supply the scalar structures in the displayed tensor products.

produces.statement: ρ:R→K is the well-defined ring map a/d↦(a in K)(d in K)⁻¹, and it factors through the identification R/pR≅𝔽_p and its natural embedding in K.

argument.text: Choose b from N003. N002 identifies M_R with R⊗_ℤ M. Define V(K)→M_R⊗_R K by m⊗c↦m⊗c, where the second occurrence of m is its image in M_R. An inverse, writing the first factor as r⊗m under N002, sends (r⊗m)⊗c to m⊗ρ(r)c. Both maps respect addition and the tensor balancing relations, since ρ extends the integer scalar map. On pure tensors their composites are identities, so they are inverse K-linear maps. For the other isomorphism send u⊗c to (u mod pM_R)⊗c. Its inverse sends (u mod pM_R)⊗c to u⊗c: a change by pz contributes pz⊗c=z⊗pc=0, and the 𝔽_p-balancing is exactly the R-balancing via F001. Again the maps are inverse on pure tensors. This proves both natural isomorphisms in the claimed directions (inverting a map where needed).

produces.statement: There are natural K-linear isomorphisms V(K)≅M_R⊗_R K≅(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{𝔽_p}K. The first sends m⊗c to m⊗c and its inverse sends (r⊗m)⊗c to m⊗ρ(r)c; the second is induced by reduction modulo pM_R.

argument.text: N003 makes (b e_i)_{i∈I} an R-basis of M_R. Apply M001 with A=R, Z=M_R, B=K (algebra map ρ), and this basis. The resulting K-basis of K⊗_R M_R is (1⊗b e_i). The flip c⊗u↦u⊗c is an isomorphism to M_R⊗_R K, since it and its inverse respect the balancing relations and are inverse on pure tensors. Composing with F002 gives a K-basis of V(K) consisting precisely of the images of (b e_i)⊗1. Also M_R/pM_R has the 𝔽_p-basis of residue classes of b e_i: expand in the R-basis and reduce each coordinate in R/pR≅𝔽_p; a vector lies in pM_R exactly when all its R-coordinates lie in pR. Thus the same basis agrees with the second scalar-extension construction, not just with the first.

produces.statement: The images of (b e_i)⊗1 in V(K) form a K-basis indexed by I. The classes of b e_i are a basis of M_R/pM_R over R/pR≅𝔽_p, and both scalar-extension identifications give those same images.

argument.text: Denote that basis by (b_i)_{i∈I}. The maps in F002 commute with each induced lattice operator, as checked on m⊗c. N001 applied to b e_i therefore gives exactly x_K b_0=0, x_K b_i=(λ−i+1)b_{i−1} for i≥1, y_K b_i=(i+1)b_{i+1} for i<λ, y_K b_λ=0, and h_K b_i=(λ−2i)b_i, with integer coefficients mapped to K. By N002 each X_r,Y_r preserves M and M_R, so its reduction X_{r,K},Y_{r,K} exists and these maps also commute with F002. For 0≤r≤λ, use M005 with q=p and a=r; H001 gives r<p, hence p∤r! and r! has nonzero image in K by the characteristic calculation in S001. The identities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r on M reduce to identities on V(K), whence X_{r,K}=(r!)⁻¹x_K^r and Y_{r,K}=(r!)⁻¹y_K^r.

produces.statement: On the K-basis b_i the x_K,y_K,h_K coefficients are the following integer coefficients mapped to K: x_K b_0=0, x_K b_i=(λ−i+1)b_{i−1} (1≤i≤λ), y_K b_i=(i+1)b_{i+1} (i<λ), y_K b_λ=0, h_K b_i=(λ−2i)b_i. The induced X_{r,K},Y_{r,K} exist for every r≥0, and for 0≤r≤λ, r!≠0 in K and X_{r,K}=(r!)⁻¹x_K^r, Y_{r,K}=(r!)⁻¹y_K^r.

argument.text: N002 gives the R-unit binom(λ,j) and the identity E_ij=binom(λ,j)⁻¹X_{λ−i}Y_λX_λY_{λ−j} on M_R. Apply scalar extension by ρ and F002. A unit maps to a unit, so the image of binom(λ,j) is nonzero. The resulting operator F_ij=ρ(binom(λ,j)⁻¹)X_{λ−i,K}Y_{λ,K}X_{λ,K}Y_{λ−j,K} sends b_j to b_i and the other b_k to zero, because E_ij(b e_k) is b e_i when k=j and zero otherwise. Thus all required matrix-unit identities persist on the basis. Together F001–F004 and this calculation prove every clause of the asserted output, existentially quantifying the chosen b and its resulting basis.

locals.declaration: Choose the K-basis β indexed by I supplied by N004; use β_i in place of its statement-bound notation b_i, with all the operator formulas stated there.
Fix any K-linear subspace W of V(K).

argument.text: Choose the basis β=(β_i)_{i∈I} in N004. H001 implies I contains 0, and N001 gives card(I)=λ+1>0, so β_0≠0 by basis independence; hence V(K)≠0. The operators x_K,y_K,h_K are the lattice-induced operators by N002 and their definitions. H002 gives the integral Chevalley bracket identities, which remain identities after scalar extension. Thus these are exactly the specified L(K)-action; being invariant under its three generators is being invariant under that Lie algebra action.

produces.statement: V(K)≠0 and x_K,y_K,h_K give its specified lattice-induced L(K)-action.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W of V(K), and assume L1: W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K. Closure of W under sums and scalar multiples, together with iteration of its x_K- and y_K-invariance, shows that it is stable under every scalar multiple of a composition of powers of x_K and y_K. N004 expresses each X_{r,K},Y_{r,K} with 0≤r≤λ in this way, since r! is invertible. All indices λ−i, λ, λ−j in its matrix-unit formula are in that range by H001. Thus W is stable under every matrix unit F_ij in N004: for every i,j∈I and every vector ∑ c_kβ_k∈W, c_jβ_i belongs to W. Only x_K and y_K were needed for this implication.

produces.statement: For every i,j∈I and every coefficient family c:I→K, if ∑_{k∈I}c_kβ_k∈W, then c_jβ_i∈W.

argument.text: By cases, either W={0}, in which case the desired disjunction holds, or W≠{0}. In the second case choose 0≠w∈W and write its unique basis expansion w=∑_{k∈I}c_kβ_k. Some c_j≠0, since otherwise w=0. For every i∈I, F002 gives c_jβ_i∈W; multiplying by c_j⁻¹ in K gives β_i∈W. Since β spans V(K), W=V(K). Both cases prove W={0} or W=V(K) under L1. Discharge L1 to obtain the implication for the arbitrary W.

produces.statement: If W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K, then W={0} or W=V(K).

argument.text: Universal introduction in W in F003, combined with F001, proves the target. The argument used only 0≤λ
